beats.say: You taste with your tongue. A butterfly tastes with its feet! Really?
Hi! I'm Pip, your nature explorer. Let's go on a bug hunt!
Yes! Butterflies have tiny tasters on their feet.
When a butterfly lands on a leaf, its feet tell it if the leaf is good.
And every butterfly starts out as a little caterpillar!
Can you flutter like a butterfly? Be gentle with every bug. See you outside, explorers!

title: Honeybees DANCE to Talk to Friends!
sources: USDA Agricultural Research Service: Honey bees

beats.say: How do bees tell their friends where the best flowers are? They dance!
Hi! I'm Pip, your nature explorer. Let's go on a bug hunt!
A honeybee does a wiggly dance called the waggle dance.
The dance shows the other bees which way to fly to find the flowers.
And bees have five eyes! Two big ones, and three tiny ones on top.
Can you do a waggle dance? Be gentle with every bug. See you outside, explorers!

title: Where Are a Snail's Eyes? Look Up!

beats.say: Your eyes are on your face. Where are a snail's eyes? Look up!
Hi! I'm Pip, your nature explorer. Let's go on a bug hunt!
A garden snail's eyes sit at the tips of its long tentacles!
It can pull them in and pop them back out. Peekaboo!
A snail slides on a slippery trail of slime. Slow and steady!
Can you slide slowly like a snail? Be gentle with every bug. See you outside, explorers!

title: Ants Can Carry Things Heavier Than Themselves!

beats.say: Could you carry a car? An ant can carry things much heavier than its own body!
Hi! I'm Pip, your nature explorer. Let's go on a bug hunt!
Ants are tiny, but they are super strong!
An ant can lift a leaf or a crumb that is heavier than itself.
And ants talk to each other with smells, and by touching their antennae.
Can you show me your strong muscles? Be gentle with every bug. See you outside, explorers!
